record.paper_title: Causal Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning: Review and Open Problems
record.original_question: How can causal inference be used to model and reduce non-stationarity in decentralized MARL when an individual agent has limited information about other agents' adapting policies and must treat their unknown behavior as a source of uncertainty or observation noise?

evidence.quote: Individual agents face a moving target problem when other agents simultaneously adapt their policies in response to observed outcomes. This non-stationarity arises from limited information about other-agent policies, which is fundamental to the multi-agent, decentralised paradigms (Papoudakis et al., 2019).

Fundamentally, non-stationarity is a source of uncertainty for individual agents. Causal inference offers tools for modelling such uncertain scenarios, especially where agents have structural knowledge of how uncertainties are arising (Lee and Bareinboim, 2020; Jesson et al., 2021).
For example, an agent may know that there is another agent in its vicinity, and it can therefore attribute (some of) the noise in its observations to the unknown behaviour policy of those agents.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a decentralized multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) setting formalized as a partially observable stochastic game with $N$ agents indexed by $i \in \{1,\dots,N\}$. The environment has state space $\mathcal{S}$, joint action space $\mathcal{A} = \prod_i \mathcal{A}_i$, transition kernel $T(s' \mid s, a_1,\dots,a_N)$, individual observation functions $O_i: \mathcal{S} \to \mathcal{O}_i$, and individual reward functions $R_i(s, a_1,\dots,a_N)$. Each agent $i$ chooses a (possibly time-varying) policy $\pi_i^t: \mathcal{O}_i \to \Delta(\mathcal{A}_i)$ based only on its own observation history, without access to the other agents' policies $\{\pi_j^t\}_{j\neq i}$ or their internal states.

From the perspective of a single agent $i$, the effective transition and reward dynamics induced by marginalizing over the unknown behaviour policies of the other agents are non-stationary: as the other agents adapt $\{\pi_j^t\}_{j\neq i}$ over time in response to observed outcomes, the conditional distribution $P^t(o_i', r_i \mid o_i, a_i)$ that agent $i$ faces changes with $t$. Assume agent $i$ has access to structural causal knowledge of the form of a directed acyclic graph $\mathcal{G}_i$ on variables $(O_i, A_i, U_{-i}, O_i', R_i)$, where $U_{-i}$ is an unobserved variable summarizing the joint policy/action of the other agents, together with the qualitative information that certain components of $U_{-i}$ are present (e.g., the agent knows another agent is in its vicinity).

Provide a principled framework, grounded in causal inference (e.g., structural causal models, do-calculus, counterfactual reasoning, or causal effect identification under unobserved confounding), that allows agent $i$ to:

(a) model the non-stationarity in $P^t(o_i', r_i \mid o_i, a_i)$ as a causal effect of the latent confounder $U_{-i}$ on its observed transitions and rewards;

(b) attribute observed observation/reward noise to the unknown behaviour policies of the other agents in a way that is consistent with $\mathcal{G}_i$;

(c) quantitatively reduce the non-stationarity-induced bias or variance in agent $i$'s policy learning, with provable guarantees (e.g., regret bounds, identifiability conditions, or sample complexity improvements) compared to a non-causal decentralized learner that treats the environment as a stationary single-agent POMDP.

Specify the assumptions on $\mathcal{G}_i$ and on the other agents' adaptation dynamics under which such guarantees can be obtained.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open research direction in the causal MARL literature. No published work appears to provide a complete, principled causal-inference framework with provable guarantees for reducing decentralized MARL non-stationarity from limited information about other agents' policies; partial progress exists on causal models for confounded bandits and single-agent RL, but a general solution remains open.

status_evidence.title: Causal Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning: Review and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Identifies causal treatment of non-stationarity in decentralized MARL as an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The framing of using causal inference to address MARL non-stationarity is listed as an open research direction.
